questions.stem: BF3 and NH3 each have three sigma bonds to the central atom. BF3 has no central lone pair; NH3 has one. Explain why three sigma bonds alone cannot determine the same central hybridisation and molecular shape for both.

difficulty.basis: Requires connecting the steric number principle (sigma bonds + lone pairs) to explain why equal sigma bonds alone do not determine hybridisation or shape.

grade9v3:analysis.common_wrong_route: Counting only sigma bonds when assigning hybridisation and shape, ignoring central lone pairs.

answer.summary: Three sigma bonds alone cannot determine the same hybridisation and shape because hybridisation depends on the total number of electron domains (steric number = sigma bonds + lone pairs). BF3 has 3 sigma bonds + 0 lone pairs = 3 domains, giving sp2 hybridisation and trigonal planar shape. NH3 has 3 sigma bonds + 1 lone pair = 4 domains, giving sp3 hybridisation and a trigonal pyramidal shape.

reasoning_route.action: Count electron domains around central atom including lone pairs.
reasoning_route.why_valid: Steric number includes both sigma bonds and lone pairs.
inputs: molecular formula and stated bonding directions

reasoning_route.action: Map steric number to introductory hybridisation: BF3 steric number is 3 (sp2); NH3 steric number is 4 (sp3).
reasoning_route.why_valid: Each electron domain occupies one hybrid orbital.
inputs: molecular formula and stated bonding directions

reasoning_route.action: Distinguish electron geometry from molecular shape: BF3 has 0 lone pairs so shape matches geometry (planar); NH3 has 1 lone pair so shape is pyramidal.
reasoning_route.why_valid: Molecular shape traces nuclei only; lone pairs do not form vertices.
inputs: molecular formula and stated bonding directions

answer.check: Verify by valence electron count: B has 3 valence electrons (3 bonding, 0 LP); N has 5 valence electrons (3 bonding, 1 LP).

Map each molecule's steric number to its introductory hybridisation set (3 -> sp2, 4 -> sp3), and observe how lone pairs affect the spatial positions of nuclei.

questions.stem: For H2C=O, assign the carbon hybridisation, count the sigma and pi components of the C=O bond, and identify the carbon orbital left available for the pi component. Keep electron-domain counting separate from counting shared electron pairs.

difficulty.basis: Requires separating shared electron pairs (4) from electron domains (3) to assign sp2, decompose C=O into 1 sigma + 1 pi, and identify the unhybridised 2p orbital.

grade9v3:analysis.common_wrong_route: Counting the double bond as two electron domains, resulting in an erroneous sp3 assignment.

answer.summary: In H2C=O, carbon has 3 electron domains (2 C-H single bonds + 1 C=O double bond) and zero lone pairs, so its hybridisation is sp2. The C=O bond consists of 1 sigma component and 1 pi component. The carbon orbital left available for the pi component is the unhybridised 2p orbital (perpendicular to the sp2 molecular plane).

reasoning_route.action: Count electron domains: 2 C-H single bonds + 1 C=O double bond = 3 domains.
reasoning_route.why_valid: A double bond acts as one electron domain in VSEPR.
inputs: molecular formula and stated bonding directions

reasoning_route.action: Assign sp2 hybridisation from 3 domains, which utilizes 2s, 2px, and 2py.
reasoning_route.why_valid: 3 domains require mixing three atomic orbitals (one s and two p).
inputs: molecular formula and stated bonding directions

reasoning_route.action: Decompose C=O double bond into 1 sigma and 1 pi component.
reasoning_route.why_valid: Double bonds consist of one coaxial sigma and one lateral pi overlap.
inputs: molecular formula and stated bonding directions

reasoning_route.action: Identify the remaining orbital as the unhybridised 2pz orbital.
reasoning_route.why_valid: Carbon has three 2p orbitals; sp2 leaves one 2p orbital unhybridised.
inputs: molecular formula and stated bonding directions

answer.check: Check orbital conservation: 1 s + 3 p = 4 valence orbitals = 3 sp2 hybrids (sigma) + 1 unhybridised p (pi).

scaffolds.text: Separate the count of total shared electron pairs from the count of electron domains: how many regions of electron density surround the central carbon?

questions.stem: Ethene is H2C=CH2. Translate this Lewis representation into a qualitative orbital-overlap diagram showing the C–C sigma framework, the two unhybridised carbon p orbitals and their side-on overlap. Label which directions are in the molecular plane and which are perpendicular to it.

difficulty.basis: Translating Lewis H2C=CH2 into a 3D orbital overlap diagram with explicit in-plane vs perpendicular directional labels.

grade9v3:analysis.common_wrong_route: Placing the unhybridised 2p orbitals or the pi bond in the molecular plane alongside the sigma bonds.

answer.summary: In ethene (H2C=CH2), all six atoms lie in the molecular plane (xy plane). The C-C sigma bond is formed by coaxial head-on overlap of C(sp2) hybrids, and four C-H sigma bonds lie in the same molecular plane. Each carbon retains one unhybridised 2p orbital (2pz) oriented perpendicular to the molecular plane (along the z axis). Side-on overlap of these parallel 2pz orbitals above and below the plane forms the pi bond, with its nodal plane coinciding with the molecular plane.

reasoning_route.action: Map ethene sigma framework into the molecular plane (xy plane).
reasoning_route.why_valid: sp2 hybrid orbitals are coplanar with 120 degree angles.
inputs: molecular formula and stated bonding directions

reasoning_route.action: Orient unhybridised 2pz orbitals perpendicular to the molecular plane.
reasoning_route.why_valid: The remaining p orbital is orthogonal to the two p orbitals used in sp2.
inputs: molecular formula and stated bonding directions

reasoning_route.action: Represent lateral pi overlap above and below the molecular plane.
reasoning_route.why_valid: Side-on overlap of parallel p lobes creates the pi bond with a nodal plane.
inputs: molecular formula and stated bonding directions

answer.check: Confirm that the nodal plane of the pi bond contains all six atomic nuclei.

scaffolds.text: Identify the molecular plane: all nuclei in ethene lie in a single plane (the xy plane). Which orbitals form the sigma backbone?

questions.stem: For CO2, connect the central-carbon Lewis domain count to its hybrid-orbital model, the number of remaining carbon p orbitals and the sigma/pi composition of its two C=O bonds. Explain how these pieces fit one consistent linear arrangement.

difficulty.basis: Synthesizes domain count (2), sp hybridisation, remaining 2 p orbitals (2py, 2pz), and two orthogonal C=O double bonds into a consistent linear structure.

grade9v3:analysis.common_wrong_route: Assuming carbon forms two double bonds in the same plane or requires sp3 to form 4 bonds.

answer.summary: In CO2, central carbon has 2 electron domains (two C=O double bonds) and zero lone pairs, producing linear sp hybridisation (180 degrees). Mixing 2s and 2px forms two collinear sp hybrids along the x-axis, creating two C-O sigma bonds. Carbon retains two unhybridised p orbitals: 2py (vertical) and 2pz (perpendicular). One C=O double bond contains a pi bond formed by 2py-2py overlap, while the other C=O double bond contains a pi bond formed by 2pz-2pz overlap. Because 2py and 2pz are mutually perpendicular, the two pi bonds occupy orthogonal planes, allowing two double bonds without orbital clash, perfectly consistent with a linear 180 degree geometry.

reasoning_route.action: Central carbon has 2 electron domains -> sp hybridisation.
reasoning_route.why_valid: Two double bonds correspond to steric number 2.
inputs: molecular formula and stated bonding directions

reasoning_route.action: Two sp hybrids form linear sigma bonds at 180 degrees along the x-axis.
reasoning_route.why_valid: sp hybridisation produces a linear arrangement.
inputs: molecular formula and stated bonding directions

reasoning_route.action: Identify the two remaining unhybridised 2p orbitals on carbon as 2py and 2pz.
reasoning_route.why_valid: Only 2px was used in sp hybridisation; 2py and 2pz remain free.
inputs: molecular formula and stated bonding directions

reasoning_route.action: Form two mutually perpendicular pi bonds with the two oxygen atoms.
reasoning_route.why_valid: 2py overlaps with one O(2py), and 2pz overlaps with the other O(2pz).
inputs: molecular formula and stated bonding directions

answer.check: Verify orbital conservation: 1 s + 1 px (sigma) + 1 py (pi_y) + 1 pz (pi_z) = 4 orbitals total.

scaffolds.text: Count the electron domains around central carbon in O=C=O. How many double bonds surround carbon, and what steric number does that correspond to?

questions.stem: Consider the claim: 'Any central atom with three sigma bonds must be sp2.' Given BF3: three B–F sigma bonds, zero boron lone pairs, planar; NH3: three N–H sigma bonds, one nitrogen lone pair, pyramidal. Decide whether these observations support the claim, give the decisive warrant, and state a more defensible introductory rule. Explain what the shape observations alone do not prove about orbitals.

difficulty.basis: Refuting a universal claim using NH3 as a counterexample, stating the correct steric number rule, and explaining the epistemic boundary of hybrid orbital models.

grade9v3:analysis.common_wrong_route: Treating hybrid orbitals as physical entities directly verified by shape observations, or believing sigma bond count alone determines hybridisation.

answer.summary: The observations DO NOT support the claim; NH3 directly refutes it. Although NH3 has three sigma bonds, its central nitrogen has one lone pair, giving steric number 4 (sp3 hybridisation, trigonal pyramidal shape). A more defensible introductory rule is: 'Central atom hybridisation is determined by total electron domains (steric number = sigma bonds + lone pairs), where steric number 3 corresponds to sp2 and steric number 4 corresponds to sp3.' Shape observations alone (measured positions of nuclei) prove molecular geometry, but do not prove that hybrid orbitals physically exist; hybridisation is a mathematical Valence Bond model constructed to rationalize observed shapes.

reasoning_route.action: Evaluate claim against NH3: NH3 has 3 sigma bonds but is sp3 and pyramidal.
reasoning_route.why_valid: A single counterexample refutes a universal claim.
inputs: molecular formula and stated bonding directions

reasoning_route.action: Identify decisive warrant: steric number (sigma + lone pairs) governs hybridisation.
reasoning_route.why_valid: Lone pairs require hybrid orbital domains alongside sigma bonds.
inputs: molecular formula and stated bonding directions

reasoning_route.action: Explain epistemic limit: shape reveals nuclear positions, not atomic orbital mixing.
reasoning_route.why_valid: Hybrid orbitals are mathematical constructs in VB theory, not spectroscopic observables.
inputs: molecular formula and stated bonding directions

answer.check: Counterexample validation: NH3 and H3O+ both have 3 sigma bonds and 1 lone pair; both are sp3 and trigonal pyramidal.

scaffolds.text: Check whether the claim is universal: can you find a central atom with three sigma bonds that is NOT sp2?
Compare BF3 (3 sigma bonds, 0 lone pairs) and NH3 (3 sigma bonds, 1 lone pair). Which molecule contradicts the claim that 3 sigma bonds must be sp2?
Formulate the correct rule using steric number (sigma + lone pairs), and consider what measured nuclear positions (shapes) do and do not prove about wavefunctions.

questions.stem: In CH3F, carbon has three C–H single bonds and one C–F single bond. Assign its introductory local hybridisation and explain why the number of electron-domain directions is unchanged from CH4 even though the attached atoms are different. Do not assume all bond properties are identical.

difficulty.basis: Explaining why electron domain directions remain 4 (sp3) in CH3F despite different substituent atoms (F vs H), while recognizing non-identical bond lengths and angles.

grade9v3:analysis.common_wrong_route: Assuming that different attached atoms require different hybridisation labels or that sp3 requires four perfectly identical bonds.

answer.summary: In CH3F, carbon has four single bonds (three C-H and one C-F) and zero lone pairs, giving introductory local hybridisation sp3. The number of electron-domain directions is unchanged from CH4 (4 directions) because each single covalent bond constitutes one localized region of electron density that repels the others, regardless of the attached atom's identity. However, because fluorine is more electronegative and larger than hydrogen, the C-F bond is more polar and longer than C-H bonds, slightly perturbing the bond angles from 109.5 degrees (C3v symmetry) without altering the 4-domain steric framework.

reasoning_route.action: Assign carbon hybridisation: 4 single bonds = 4 electron domains -> sp3.
reasoning_route.why_valid: Steric number 4 corresponds to sp3 hybridisation.
inputs: molecular formula and stated bonding directions

reasoning_route.action: Explain domain invariance: each single bond is one domain of mutual repulsion regardless of atom identity.
reasoning_route.why_valid: VSEPR domain count is based on number of bonded atoms and lone pairs.
inputs: molecular formula and stated bonding directions

reasoning_route.action: Acknowledge bond property differences: C-F polarity and length perturb bond angles away from ideal 109.5 degrees.
reasoning_route.why_valid: Differing electronegativities alter electron distribution without changing domain count.
inputs: molecular formula and stated bonding directions

answer.check: Verify that total valence electrons around carbon equal 8 (octet satisfied via 4 sigma bonds).

scaffolds.text: Look at the number of bonding directions around carbon in CH3F: does each single bond count as one electron domain regardless of the attached atom?
In VSEPR theory, each region of localized bonding electron density repels other regions. How many single bonds connect to carbon in CH3F compared to CH4?
Recognise that domain count (4) fixes the introductory sp3 label, while differences in electronegativity between F and H alter polarity and bond angles.

questions.stem: HCN is represented as H–C≡N with a lone pair on nitrogen. Assign the introductory hybridisation at carbon and nitrogen, and count the sigma and pi components of the C≡N bond. Explain how the local domain count is compatible with those components.

difficulty.basis: Assigning hybridisation at both C and N in H-C#N, breaking down C#N into 1 sigma + 2 pi, and showing domain compatibility at both atoms.

grade9v3:analysis.common_wrong_route: Counting the triple bond as 3 domains or failing to hybridise terminal nitrogen.

answer.summary: In HCN (H-C≡N:), Carbon has 2 electron domains (1 C-H single bond + 1 C≡N triple bond) and zero lone pairs -> sp hybridised. Nitrogen has 2 electron domains (1 C≡N triple bond + 1 lone pair) -> sp hybridised. The C≡N triple bond consists of 1 sigma component and 2 pi components. This is fully compatible with the local domain counts: at each atom, 2 sp hybrids form the sigma framework (and accommodate N's lone pair), leaving two unhybridised 2p orbitals on each atom to form the two mutually perpendicular pi bonds.

reasoning_route.action: Count domains: C has 2 domains (sp); N has 2 domains (sp).
reasoning_route.why_valid: Triple bond = 1 domain; N lone pair = 1 domain.
inputs: molecular formula and stated bonding directions

reasoning_route.action: Decompose C#N into 1 sigma bond and 2 pi bonds.
reasoning_route.why_valid: A triple bond always comprises 1 coaxial sigma and 2 lateral pi bonds.
inputs: molecular formula and stated bonding directions

reasoning_route.action: Show orbital compatibility: 2 sp hybrids form sigma/lone pair, leaving two 2p orbitals per atom for 2 pi bonds.
reasoning_route.why_valid: sp hybridisation conserves two unhybridised p orbitals for pi bonding.
inputs: molecular formula and stated bonding directions

answer.check: Check orbital counts on both atoms: C has 2 sp + 2 p = 4; N has 2 sp + 2 p = 4.

scaffolds.text: Count the electron domains at each individual atom: how many domains surround carbon, and how many surround nitrogen?
A triple bond counts as 1 domain. Carbon has 1 single bond + 1 triple bond (2 domains); Nitrogen has 1 triple bond + 1 lone pair (2 domains).

questions.stem: For methylamine, CH3–NH2, carbon has four single bonds and nitrogen has three single bonds plus a lone pair. Compare the introductory local hybridisation and arrangement of bonded atoms at carbon and nitrogen. Explain why the same hybridisation label does not require identical molecular shapes.

difficulty.basis: Comparing C and N in CH3-NH2: both sp3, but C has a tetrahedral arrangement of bonded atoms while N has a trigonal pyramidal arrangement, explaining why identical hybridisation does not require identical molecular shapes.

grade9v3:analysis.common_wrong_route: Equating hybridisation label directly with molecular shape, assuming all sp3 centres must be tetrahedral.

answer.summary: In methylamine (CH3-NH2), Carbon has 4 single bonds and 0 lone pairs (steric number 4) -> sp3 hybridisation, tetrahedral arrangement of bonded atoms. Nitrogen has 3 single bonds and 1 lone pair (steric number 4) -> sp3 hybridisation, trigonal pyramidal arrangement of bonded atoms. The same hybridisation label does not require identical molecular shapes because hybridisation reflects the total electron-domain geometry (all electron pairs), whereas molecular shape describes only the spatial arrangement of the atomic nuclei. Nitrogen's lone pair occupies a hybrid orbital but does not contribute an atomic vertex, reducing the visible shape from tetrahedral to trigonal pyramidal.

reasoning_route.action: Assign hybridisation: C has 4 domains (sp3); N has 4 domains (sp3).
reasoning_route.why_valid: Steric number is 4 for both centres.
inputs: molecular formula and stated bonding directions

reasoning_route.action: Compare bonded atom arrangements: C is tetrahedral; N is trigonal pyramidal.
reasoning_route.why_valid: C has 4 bonded atoms; N has 3 bonded atoms.
inputs: molecular formula and stated bonding directions

reasoning_route.action: Explain shape discrepancy: molecular shape describes nuclei only, not non-bonding pairs.
reasoning_route.why_valid: Lone pairs occupy space in electron geometry without appearing as nuclear vertices in molecular shape.
inputs: molecular formula and stated bonding directions

answer.check: Contrast bond angles: H-C-H is close to 109.5 degrees; H-N-H is compressed to approx 106-107 degrees by lone pair repulsion.

Explain why molecular shape considers nuclear vertices only, while hybridisation reflects all valence electron pairs (including non-bonding lone pairs).

questions.stem: A carbon centre has three sigma-bond directions, no lone pair, and participates in one pi bond. Translate this description into a qualitative local orbital arrangement and check that the orbitals used in the sigma and pi parts have not been counted twice.

difficulty.basis: Translating 3 sigma directions, 0 LP, 1 pi bond into an sp2 + unhybridised p representation and verifying that orbital accounting strictly conserves 4 valence orbitals without double counting.

grade9v3:analysis.common_wrong_route: Assuming carbon uses sp3 hybridisation while also forming a pi bond, which would erroneously require 5 valence orbitals (4 sp3 + 1 p).

answer.summary: For a carbon centre with 3 sigma-bond directions, 0 lone pairs, and 1 pi bond: Carbon mixes one 2s and two 2p orbitals (e.g. 2px, 2py) to form three equivalent sp2 hybrid orbitals directed in a plane at 120 degrees for sigma bonding. One 2p orbital (2pz) remains unhybridised and oriented perpendicular to the sp2 plane, participating in side-on pi overlap. Orbital accounting check: 1(2s) + 2(2p) = 3 sp2 hybrid orbitals (used in sigma bonds); 1(2p) = 1 unhybridised p orbital (used in pi bond). Total orbitals = 3 + 1 = 4 atomic orbitals. Exactly 4 valence atomic orbitals entered the model and 4 are accounted for; no orbital is counted twice.

reasoning_route.action: Represent sigma framework as three sp2 hybrid orbitals at 120 degrees.
reasoning_route.why_valid: Three planar sigma directions require sp2 hybridisation.
inputs: molecular formula and stated bonding directions

reasoning_route.action: Represent pi bond as one unhybridised 2p orbital perpendicular to the sp2 plane.
reasoning_route.why_valid: Pi bonding requires an unhybridised p orbital orthogonal to the sigma plane.
inputs: molecular formula and stated bonding directions

reasoning_route.action: Perform orbital conservation check: 3 sp2 hybrids + 1 unhybridised p = 4 valence orbitals.
reasoning_route.why_valid: Carbon has exactly 4 valence orbitals (one 2s and three 2p); all are accounted for without double-counting.
inputs: molecular formula and stated bonding directions

answer.check: Verify that 4 input atomic orbitals (s, px, py, pz) yield exactly 4 output orbitals (3 sp2 + 1 pz).

questions.stem: A student says, 'If the electron-domain geometry is tetrahedral, the atoms must form a tetrahedral molecular shape.' Evaluate the statement using CH4, NH3 and H2O, with their respective central lone-pair counts of zero, one and two.

difficulty.basis: Evaluating the student statement using CH4 (0 LP, tetrahedral), NH3 (1 LP, pyramidal), and H2O (2 LP, bent), proving the statement is false and providing the decisive warrant.

grade9v3:analysis.common_wrong_route: Conflating electron-domain geometry with molecular shape, assuming that domain geometry dictates shape regardless of lone pairs.

answer.summary: The student's statement is FALSE. While CH4, NH3, and H2O all have tetrahedral electron-domain geometry (steric number 4), their molecular shapes differ based on central lone pair counts: CH4 (0 lone pairs) has 4 bonded atoms -> tetrahedral molecular shape; NH3 (1 lone pair) has 3 bonded atoms -> trigonal pyramidal molecular shape; H2O (2 lone pairs) has 2 bonded atoms -> bent / angular molecular shape. Decisive warrant: Electron-domain geometry describes the arrangement of all electron pairs (bonding + non-bonding), whereas molecular shape describes exclusively the spatial arrangement of atomic nuclei. Shape matches domain geometry only when the central atom has zero lone pairs.

reasoning_route.action: Evaluate the statement as false by comparing CH4, NH3, and H2O.
reasoning_route.why_valid: NH3 and H2O serve as direct counterexamples to the claim.
inputs: molecular formula and stated bonding directions

reasoning_route.action: Map each molecule: CH4 is tetrahedral, NH3 is trigonal pyramidal, H2O is bent.
reasoning_route.why_valid: Positions of nuclei define molecular shape.
inputs: molecular formula and stated bonding directions

reasoning_route.action: State decisive warrant: electron geometry tracks all domains; shape tracks nuclei only.
reasoning_route.why_valid: Non-bonding lone pairs occupy domain vertices without creating visible atomic vertices in molecular shape.
inputs: molecular formula and stated bonding directions

answer.check: Test with another 4-domain species: H3O+ has 1 lone pair and is trigonal pyramidal; NH4+ has 0 lone pairs and is tetrahedral.

scaffolds.text: Analyze the student statement: is molecular shape always identical to electron-domain geometry, or only under specific conditions?

State the decisive warrant: electron-domain geometry tracks all electron pairs, but molecular shape tracks atomic nuclei only. Formulate the general rule.
